items.description: Verify schedule_tasks returns correct ordering for linear dependency chain
items.expected_behavior: Given tasks [fetch_data, clean_data, train_model, evaluate_model] with linear dependencies, function returns [fetch_data, clean_data, train_model, evaluate_model]

items.description: Verify long dependency chain execution
items.expected_behavior: Long linear chain of dependencies is correctly ordered respecting all constraints

items.description: Verify ValueError on duplicate task names
items.expected_behavior: Function raises ValueError when tasks list contains duplicate names

items.description: Verify ValueError on unknown task in dependency
items.expected_behavior: Function raises ValueError when dependency references a task not in tasks list

items.description: Verify ValueError on circular dependency
items.expected_behavior: Function raises ValueError when circular dependency exists (e.g., A→B→C→A)

items.description: Verify TypeError when tasks is not a list
items.expected_behavior: Function raises TypeError when tasks parameter is not a list (e.g., tuple, string, dict)

items.description: Verify TypeError when dependencies is not a list
items.expected_behavior: Function raises TypeError when dependencies parameter is not a list

items.description: Verify TypeError when task name is not a string
items.expected_behavior: Function raises TypeError when any task name is not a string (e.g., int, None, list)

items.description: Verify TypeError when dependency is not a pair of strings
items.expected_behavior: Function raises TypeError when dependency tuple is not a pair or contains non-string elements

items.description: Verify case-sensitive task name handling
items.expected_behavior: Task names 'Task' and 'task' are treated as distinct tasks

items.description: Verify function does not execute tasks or modify external state
items.expected_behavior: Function returns ordering only; no side effects, file operations, or task execution occur

items.description: Verify lexicographic ordering when no dependencies exist
items.expected_behavior: Given tasks [b, a, c] with empty dependencies, function returns [c, b, a] (lexicographically largest first)

items.description: Verify self-referential dependency is rejected
items.expected_behavior: Function raises ValueError when a task has a dependency on itself (A→A)

items.description: Verify every task appears exactly once in output
items.expected_behavior: Output list contains all input tasks with no duplicates and length equals input task count

items.description: Verify dependency ordering constraint is satisfied
items.expected_behavior: For every dependency pair (A, B), A appears at an earlier index than B in the output

items.description: Verify deterministic output on multiple valid orderings
items.expected_behavior: Multiple calls with same inputs return identical ordering; lexicographic selection ensures determinism

items.description: Verify diamond-shaped dependency graph handling
items.expected_behavior: Given tasks [a, b, c, d] with diamond dependencies, function returns valid ordering where a precedes b and c, and both b and c precede d

items.description: Verify multiple independent dependency chains
items.expected_behavior: Independent chains are ordered deterministically via lexicographic availability; all dependencies within chains are respected

items.description: Verify empty input returns empty list
items.expected_behavior: Given empty tasks list and empty dependencies, function returns []

items.description: Verify single task with no dependencies
items.expected_behavior: Given single task and no dependencies, function returns list containing that task

summary: The schedule_tasks(tasks: list[str], dependencies: list[tuple[str, str]]) function computes a valid topological ordering of tasks respecting all dependency constraints. Core success behavior: every task appears exactly once, all dependency pairs (A, B) have A before B, and when multiple tasks are available, lexicographically largest is selected first for deterministic output. Main error cases: ValueError for duplicate tasks, unknown task references, or circular dependencies; TypeError for non-list inputs or non-string task names.
